r25q_03de4560229f9c671b.explanation: The match-control index identifies the Lily Brooks over-33 review as the Brooks-Price delivery, the commentary reconciliation equates it with the pavilion-end entry, the routing note files that entry under the 16:12 signal review (pavilion folio 38), which links to the signed scorer sheet at folio 38, row 20, carried forward as pre-lock ledger cell 38/20-Q, so only that cell's observations apply. The bowler's-end umpire signalled No ball, so the delivery is a No-ball that does not count in the over; the boundary resulted from a fielder's throw at the wicket with the agreed 4-run allowance, and for the two conflicting signed running entries the protocol uses the greatest revision number, so the batters had crossed when the throw left the fielder and the run in progress was completed, making 4 batter runs plus the 1 No-ball extra (5 total; bowler charged 5). The throw-at-the-wicket cannot yield a Run out because the batters were in their ground on completion. Counterfactually, changing only the running observation so the batters had not crossed at the instant of the throw removes the run in progress under Law 19.8, leaving 4 batter runs plus the 1 No-ball extra (5 total runs, bowler 6), with every other fact and source selection unchanged.

r25q_5d6660d0423190d267.explanation: The match-control index identifies the Sophie Blake over-20 review as the Blake-Shaw delivery, the commentary reconciliation equates it with the pavilion-end entry, and the routing note files that entry under the 11:22 signal review (pavilion folio 22), so only that review's observations apply. The ball touched neither bat nor person, no No-ball or Wide call is recorded, the striker was not attempting a run, the batter was out of ground, the wicket-keeper alone fairly put down the wicket, the fielding side appealed in time, and the ball was live, so Stumped is complete under Law 39.1 (Run out is excluded because the striker was not attempting a run) and no runs are scored. Counterfactually, changing only the running observation so the striker was attempting a run removes the Stumped precondition; with the ball live and the wicket fairly put down out of ground, the dismissal becomes Run out under Laws 38.1-38.2, with the scoring record unchanged at zero runs.

r25q_c8f34a28b50497329e.explanation: The match-control index identifies the Zoe Turner over-26 review as the Turner-Moore delivery, the commentary reconciliation equates it with the pavilion-end entry, and the routing note files that entry under the 14:53 signal review linked to the signed scorer sheet at folio 12, row 6, so only that sheet's observations apply. The review lock was 18:25 and the protocol uses the latest signed entry at or before the lock, so the audio-log observation that the ball was already dead when the wicket was broken governs over the conflicting live-ball claim. Under Laws 20.1 and 20.6 the later broken wicket cannot create a dismissal, so the Run out submission fails; the 1 completed run before the terminal event stands as a batter run (the post-event loose-ball boundary is not scored), giving 1 batter run, 1 bowler run, and 1 total run. Counterfactually, changing only that observation so the ball was still live when the wicket was broken makes the Run out complete under Laws 38.1-38.2 (batter out of ground, wicket fairly put down, timely appeal); the completed run is still recorded, so the ledger keeps 1 batter run, 1 bowler run, and 1 total run, with every other fact and source selection unchanged.

r25q_dac4d9ea797c8631a1.explanation: The match-control index identifies the Hannah Cole over-34 review as the Cole-Hayes delivery, and the commentary reconciliation identifies it with the pavilion-end entry, so only that entry's observations apply. The worksheet records bat contact and the umpire signal sheet records a 4-run agreed boundary allowance coming directly from the delivery (not an overthrow), with no No-ball or Wide call and no wicket event, so the delivery is legal, the 4 runs are batter runs, and no dismissal applies. Bowler runs equal batter runs (4) since there are no No-ball or Wide extras. Counterfactually, changing only the agreed boundary allowance to 6 makes the bat-struck boundary worth 6 batter runs (Laws 19.6-19.7), giving 6 batter runs, 6 bowler runs, and 6 total runs, with every other fact unchanged.

r25q_fef23ec11ccb5c6c3b.explanation: The match-control index identifies the Ella Foster over-14 review as the Foster-Bennett delivery, the commentary reconciliation equates it with the pavilion-end entry, and the routing note files that entry under the 18:58 signal review (pavilion folio 15), so only that review's observations apply. The ball touched the striker's bat, did not touch the ground before control, there was no boundary contact before control was complete, the fielder controlled both ball and movement, the fielding side appealed in time, and the wicket event was submitted as Caught, so the caught dismissal stands under Laws 33.1-33.3 and no runs are scored; the recorded 4-run boundary allowance is inoperative because the catch completed before any boundary contact. Counterfactually, changing only the contact observation so the fielder touched the boundary while carrying the ball before completing control means no fair catch was completed, so the dismissal fails and the delivery is scored off the bat as a four (batter runs 4, bowler runs 4, total 4), with every other fact unchanged.
